text: A full, illustrative case study — Brightleaf Outfitters, a fictional retailer used purely as a realistic scenario. A revenue report is off by two hundred thousand dollars. We'll trace it using everything from the last four chapters.

Finance flags that the revenue report shows 2.1 million, but the point of sale system's own daily totals add up to roughly 2.3 million. The report has looked fine for over a year. Nobody currently on the team built the original pipeline.

The analyst walks the lineage hop by hop — POS transactions, a nightly extraction, a cleaning transformation, a warehouse load, the dashboard tile. At the column level, the filter condition excluding 'voided' transactions turns out to also be excluding legitimate after-hours sales, because of a POS-side labeling change nobody told the data team about.

Before fixing anything, the analyst checks what else reads from that same transformation step — three other reports depend on it, so this bug has been quietly affecting revenue, inventory, and commissions everywhere downstream. The fix fixes the filter condition, and updates the lineage record itself to document the fragile dependency.
Next up: a second case study — this time tracing customer data across multiple systems, where the problem isn't a wrong number, but duplicate and inconsistent records.
